missing_spec_content.spec_text: Some LICs and NEEs are experiencing rapid economic development which leads to significant social, environmental and cultural change.
missing_spec_content.why: Social and environmental change are covered. Cultural change caused by development is not taught as an effect of development. Nollywood and music appear only as industries and as global importance. Ethnic and religious groups appear only as background context, not as things that are changing.

factual_errors.text: In 2025 services made up about 58% of Nigeria's economy, industry about 16% and farming about 23%.
factual_errors.correction: In the World Bank data used, 'industry' (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS) includes oil and gas extraction, construction and utilities as well as manufacturing. The same key point classes oil as primary ('The primary sector takes raw materials from the land or sea: farming, fishing, oil'). Students will therefore wrongly read 16% as the secondary or manufacturing share and 23% as the whole primary sector. In this classification, farming 23% is only part of the primary sector, and oil sits inside the 16%.

factual_errors.text: Unilever makes soap, food and drinks in factories in Nigeria.
factual_errors.correction: In 2023 Unilever Nigeria announced it was leaving the home care and skin cleansing categories (which include soaps and detergents) to focus on personal care, beauty and food. The claim that it makes soap in Nigeria is out of date. The 'drinks' claim is also doubtful, as Unilever sold its tea business in 2022. The same claim appears in keyPoints[2].writeBullets: 'Unilever: soap and food factories'.

Exact values of the sourced World Bank figures dated 2025 or 2024 could not be confirmed: population about 238 million, GDP about $291 billion, GNI per head $1,360, fuel about 86% of goods exports, sector shares 58/16/23% and farming about 34% of jobs. The 2025 GDP and sector shares in particular depend on Nigeria's 2025 GDP rebasing.

Life expectancy (47 in 2000, 55 in 2024) and infant mortality (95 in 2000, 70 in 2024): these are plausible but the exact values could not be checked. Some published series give a higher infant mortality figure for 2000.

Shell figure: completion date of the SPDC sale to Renaissance Africa Energy Company (13 March 2025) and current Bonga deep-water operations. Taken from the cited source and consistent with my knowledge, but not checked against the live page.
